audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for final charge, preach/proclaim, itching ears, poured out, good fight, abandonment, rescue, greetings.

verses.restored: I solemnly testify before the Divine and Messiah Jesus, the One about to judge living and dead, and by his appearing and his reign:

familiar.text: I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

modern.text: I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:

original.text: ⸀Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃, τοῦ μέλλοντος κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, ⸀καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: proclaim the word; stand ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, encourage, with all patience and teaching.

familiar.text: Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.

modern.text: Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction.

original.text: κήρυξον τὸν λόγον, ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως, ἔλεγξον, ἐπιτίμησον, παρακάλεσον, ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ.

verses.restored: For there will be a season when they will not endure healthy teaching, but according to their own desires they will heap up teachers for themselves, itching in hearing,

familiar.text: For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;

modern.text: For the time will come when men will not tolerate sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires.

original.text: ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ⸂ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας⸃ ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν,

verses.restored: and indeed they will turn hearing away from the truth and will turn aside to myths.

familiar.text: And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.

modern.text: So they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.

original.text: καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν, ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται.

verses.restored: But you be sober in all things, endure hardship, do work of one announcing good news, fulfill your service.

familiar.text: But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry.

modern.text: But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.

original.text: σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν, κακοπάθησον, ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ, τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον.

verses.restored: For I am already being poured out, and the season of my departure has stood near.

familiar.text: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.

modern.text: For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.

original.text: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἤδη σπένδομαι, καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ⸂ἀναλύσεώς μου⸃ ἐφέστηκεν.

verses.restored: I have struggled the beautiful/good struggle; I have completed the course; I have kept the trust.

familiar.text: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

modern.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

original.text: τὸν ⸂καλὸν ἀγῶνα⸃ ἠγώνισμαι, τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα, τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα·

verses.restored: From now on the crown of righteousness/justice is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous/just judge, will repay to me in that day, and not only to me but also to all those having loved his appearing.

familiar.text: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.

modern.text: From now on there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing. Personal Concerns

original.text: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος, ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ὁ δίκαιος κριτής, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Be eager to come to me quickly,

familiar.text: Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me:

modern.text: Make every effort to come to me quickly,

original.text: Σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με ταχέως·

verses.restored: for Demas, having loved the present age, abandoned me and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.

familiar.text: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.

modern.text: because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

original.text: Δημᾶς γάρ με ⸀ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν, Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν·

verses.restored: Luke alone is with me. Taking Mark, bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.

familiar.text: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.

modern.text: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.

original.text: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετʼ ἐμοῦ. Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ, ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν,

verses.restored: But Tychicus I sent to Ephesus.

familiar.text: And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus.

modern.text: Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.

original.text: Τυχικὸν δὲ ἀπέστειλα εἰς Ἔφεσον.

verses.restored: The cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, bring when you come, and the scrolls, especially the parchments.

familiar.text: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.

modern.text: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.

original.text: τὸν φαιλόνην, ὃν ⸀ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ, ἐρχόμενος φέρε, καὶ τὰ βιβλία, μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας.

verses.restored: Alexander the metalworker did many harmful things to me; the Lord will repay him according to his works.

familiar.text: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:

modern.text: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.

original.text: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο— ⸀ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ—

verses.restored: You also guard yourself from him, for he greatly opposed our words.

familiar.text: Of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.

modern.text: You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message. The Lord Remains Faithful

original.text: ὃν καὶ σὺ φυλάσσου, λίαν γὰρ ⸀ἀντέστη τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις.

verses.restored: At my first defense no one came alongside me, but all abandoned me; may it not be counted against them.

familiar.text: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.

modern.text: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.

original.text: Ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μου ἀπολογίᾳ οὐδείς μοι ⸀παρεγένετο, ἀλλὰ πάντες με ⸀ἐγκατέλιπον— μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη—

verses.restored: But the Lord stood by me and empowered me, so that through me the proclamation might be fulfilled and all the nations might hear; and I was rescued from lion's mouth.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.

modern.text: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.

original.text: ὁ δὲ κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με, ἵνα διʼ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ⸀ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος.

verses.restored: The Lord will rescue me from every harmful work and save/heal me into his heavenly reign; to him be glory into the ages of the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

modern.text: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen. Final Greetings (Ephesians 6:21–24; Philippians 4:21–23)

original.text: ⸀ῥύσεταί με ὁ κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.

verses.restored: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.

familiar.text: Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.

modern.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, as well as the household of Onesiphorus.

original.text: Ἄσπασαι Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν καὶ τὸν Ὀνησιφόρου οἶκον.

verses.restored: Erastus remained in Corinth, but Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.

familiar.text: Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick.

modern.text: Erastus has remained at Corinth, and Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.

original.text: Ἔραστος ἔμεινεν ἐν Κορίνθῳ, Τρόφιμον δὲ ⸀ἀπέλιπον ἐν Μιλήτῳ ἀσθενοῦντα.

verses.restored: Be eager to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the siblings.

familiar.text: Do thy diligence to come before winter. Eubulus greeteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren.

modern.text: Make every effort to come to me before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.

original.text: Σπούδασον πρὸ χειμῶνος ἐλθεῖν. Ἀσπάζεταί σε Εὔβουλος καὶ Πούδης καὶ Λίνος καὶ Κλαυδία καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.

verses.restored: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.

familiar.text: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

modern.text: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

original.text: Ὁ ⸀κύριος μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματός σου. ἡ χάρις μεθʼ ⸀ὑμῶν.

translation_notes: Final charge is proclamation with patience and teaching, not domination.
The crown of righteousness/justice is linked to faithful endurance and longing for appearing.
Paul's prayer that abandonment not be counted against them preserves mercy even in loneliness.
